end

return PanelSizes

--[[
	PanelStack  -  keeps the floating panels in the order they were last used: the panel last
	pressed, dragged or opened draws over the others.
	Loaded by Widgets.luau; receives the shared W table and adds:
	  W.watchPanelStack(screenGui)         starts the ordering for a ScreenGui's top-level panels
	  W.raisePanel(panel)                  brings a stacked panel to the front
	  W.getPanelOrder()                    the stacked panels, least recently used first
	  W.linkPanelBackground(panel, image)  called by Widgets.attachPanelBackground: the sibling
	                                       image stays one layer under its panel
	Stacked: every direct child of the ScreenGui that is a GuiObject but not a button, whose
	ZIndex is from 1 to POPUP_FLOOR - 1 once it has been added. Its ZIndex is this module's from then on.
	Not stacked: anything built with a ZIndex of POPUP_FLOOR or more (menus, modal dialogs and
	their backdrops, toasts, option lists, the Config and Hit Filter panels). Those stay over every
	panel, so a new popup keeps its ZIndex at POPUP_FLOOR or above and a new floating panel below it.
	Layers run downward from POPUP_FLOOR - 2, two per showing panel: the panel, then its
	background image.
	Mutates: ZIndex of the live top-level panels and of their background images. Nothing is saved.
	Refreshed by: a mouse press over a panel, a panel becoming visible.
	PanelPush reads the list to learn which panels there are, and is told through
	W.requestPanelPush() every time the layers are handed out.
]]

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local POPUP_FLOOR = 20
local TOP_LAYER = POPUP_FLOOR - 2
local BACKGROUND_NAME = "PanelBackgroundImage"

return function(W)
	local gui = nil
	-- Stacked panels, least recently used first.
	local order = {}
	local stacked = {}
	local backgroundOf = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
	local isBackground = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

	-- Hands out the layers, the most recently used showing panel on top. Panels that have left
	-- the ScreenGui (a rebuilt or destroyed panel) are dropped on the way.
	local function applyLayers()
		local layer = TOP_LAYER
		for index = #order, 1, -1 do
			local panel = order[index]
			if panel.Parent ~= gui then
				table.remove(order, index)
				stacked[panel] = nil
			elseif panel.Visible then
				panel.ZIndex = layer
				local background = backgroundOf[panel]
				if background then
					background.ZIndex = layer - 1
				end
				layer -= 2
			end
		end
		W.requestPanelPush()
	end

	-- The live list: PanelPush reads it and must not change it.
	function W.getPanelOrder()
		return order
	end

	function W.raisePanel(panel)
		if not stacked[panel] then
			return
		end
		local index = table.find(order, panel)
		if index then
			table.remove(order, index)
		end
		table.insert(order, panel)
		applyLayers()
	end

	function W.linkPanelBackground(panel, image)
		backgroundOf[panel] = image
		isBackground[image] = true
		if stacked[panel] then
			image.ZIndex = panel.ZIndex - 1
		end
	end

	local function adopt(child)
		if stacked[child] or isBackground[child] or child.Parent ~= gui then
			return
		end
		if not child:IsA("GuiObject") or child:IsA("GuiButton") or child.Name == BACKGROUND_NAME then
			return
		end
		if child.ZIndex < 1 or child.ZIndex >= POPUP_FLOOR then
			return
		end
		stacked[child] = true
		table.insert(order, child)
		table.insert(W.getUISConnections(), child:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
			if child.Visible then
				W.raisePanel(child)
			end
		end))
		if child.Visible then
			applyLayers()
		end
	end

	local function contains(object, point)
		local origin = object.AbsolutePosition
		local size = object.AbsoluteSize
		return point.X >= origin.X and point.Y >= origin.Y and point.X <= origin.X + size.X and point.Y <= origin.Y + size.Y
	end

	-- The top-level object drawn last at `point`: the highest ZIndex, the later sibling on a tie.
	-- A popup or a modal backdrop over a panel is found first, so a press on it raises nothing.
	local function topmostAt(point)
		local best = nil
		for _, child in ipairs(gui:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("GuiObject") and child.Visible and not isBackground[child] and contains(child, point) then
				if best == nil or child.ZIndex >= best.ZIndex then
					best = child
				end
			end
		end
		return best
	end

	function W.watchPanelStack(screenGui)
		gui = screenGui
		order = {}
		stacked = {}
		for _, child in ipairs(gui:GetChildren()) do
			adopt(child)
		end
		local connections = W.getUISConnections()
		table.insert(connections, gui.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
			-- Deferred: a builder sets ZIndex and Visible around the line that parents the frame.
			task.defer(adopt, child)
		end))
		table.insert(connections, UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
			local kind = input.UserInputType
			if kind ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 and kind ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton2 then
				return
			end
			if not gui.Enabled then
				return
			end
			local top = topmostAt(UserInputService:GetMouseLocation())
			if top and stacked[top] then
				W.raisePanel(top)
			end
		end))
	end
end

--[[
	PropertiesShell  -  the Properties panel's frame around its list: padding, title bar, close
	button, search field and the scrolling list.
	PropertiesShell.build(W, panel) -> { header, closeButton, searchWrap, searchBox, scroll, top,
	collapsedHeight, arrowPosition, scrollbar }
	  header           frame the tabs view and the collapse arrow add their controls to
	  top              y of the search field: where the tabs view starts
	  collapsedHeight  panel height when collapsed to its title bar
	  scrollbar        { thickness, gap } of the list outside Classic (nil in Classic); the tabs
	                   view gives its own scrolling area the same, so both stand clear of the bar
	The Classic mode builds the original boxed header; the other modes build a title bar that
	spans the panel.
]]

local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local T = C.T
local LAYOUT = C.LAYOUT

local PropertiesShell = {}

-- Outside the Classic mode: the scrollbar's thickness, and the gap between it and the rows.
local SCROLLBAR = 3
local SCROLLBAR_GAP = 4

local function makeSearchBox(W, searchWrap, inset)
	local searchBox = Instance.new("TextBox")
	searchBox.Name = "SearchBox"
	searchBox.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	searchBox.Text = ""
	searchBox.PlaceholderText = "Search properties..."
	searchBox.TextColor3 = T.BrightGold
	searchBox.PlaceholderColor3 = T.DarkGold
	searchBox.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	searchBox.ClearTextOnFocus = false
	searchBox.Position = UDim2.new(0, inset, 0, 0)
	searchBox.Size = UDim2.new(1, -inset * 2, 1, 0)
	searchBox.BorderSizePixel = 0
	searchBox.Parent = searchWrap
	W.wireFieldStates(searchWrap, searchBox)
	return searchBox
end

local function makeScroll(W, panel, top, thickness, gap)
	local scroll = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
	scroll.Name = "Content"
	scroll.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	scroll.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, top)
	scroll.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -top)
	scroll.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	scroll.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	scroll.ScrollBarThickness = thickness
	scroll.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
	scroll.BorderSizePixel = 0
	scroll.Parent = panel
	table.insert(W.getThemed().scrollbars, scroll)
	W.addListLayout(scroll, gap)
	return scroll
end

local function makeDragHandle(W, panel, header)
	local dragHandle = Instance.new("TextButton")
	dragHandle.Name = "DragHandle"
	dragHandle.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	dragHandle.Text = ""
	dragHandle.Size = UDim2.new(1, -24, 1, 0)
	dragHandle.ZIndex = 2
	dragHandle.Parent = header
	W.makeDraggable(panel, dragHandle)

-- The original shell: a boxed header, a search box under it, then the list.
local function buildClassic(W, panel)
	W.addPadding(panel, 6, 6, 6, 6)
	local header = W.makeBlob("Header", panel, UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 26))

	local title = Instance.new("TextLabel")

	title.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left

	title.Position = UDim2.new(0, 8, 0, 0)
	TypeScale.style(title, "Title")
	title.Parent = header

	local closeButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
	closeButton.Name = "Close"
	closeButton.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	closeButton.Text = "X"
	closeButton.TextColor3 = T.DarkGold
	closeButton.Size = UDim2.new(0, 20, 1, 0)
	closeButton.Position = UDim2.new(1, -22, 0, 0)
	closeButton.ZIndex = 3
	TypeScale.style(closeButton, "Title")
	closeButton.Parent = header
	makeDragHandle(W, panel, header)

	local searchWrap = W.makeBlob("SearchWrap", panel, UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 20))
	searchWrap.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 28)
	local searchBox = makeSearchBox(W, searchWrap, 4)
	TypeScale.style(searchBox, "Caption")

	return {
		header = header,
		closeButton = closeButton,
		searchWrap = searchWrap,
		searchBox = searchBox,

		collapsedHeight = 38,
		arrowPosition = UDim2.new(1, -36, 0, 0),

end

-- Title bar spanning the panel edge to edge, above the padded content. A filled bar rounds its
-- top with the panel; SquareBottom squares off the lower corners.
local function makeTitleBar(W, panel, pad)
	local titleBar = Instance.new("Frame")
	titleBar.Name = "TitleBar"
	titleBar.BorderSizePixel = 0
	titleBar.Position = UDim2.new(0, -pad, 0, -pad)
	titleBar.Size = UDim2.new(1, pad * 2, 0, LAYOUT.TitleBar)
	titleBar.Parent = panel
	if C.MODE.Structure.TitleBarFill then
		W.paint(titleBar, "BackgroundColor3", "Header")
		W.addCorner(titleBar, T.BigCorner)
		local squareBottom = Instance.new("Frame")
		squareBottom.Name = "SquareBottom"
		squareBottom.BorderSizePixel = 0
		squareBottom.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0.5, 0)
		squareBottom.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0.5, 0)
		W.paint(squareBottom, "BackgroundColor3", "Header")
		squareBottom.Parent = titleBar
	else
		titleBar.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	end

	local rule = Instance.new("Frame")
	rule.Name = "Rule"
	rule.BorderSizePixel = 0
	rule.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, -1)
	rule.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1)
	W.paint(rule, "BackgroundColor3", "PanelStroke")
	rule.Parent = titleBar
end

local function buildModern(W, panel)
	local pad = LAYOUT.PanelPad
	W.addPadding(panel, pad, pad, pad, pad)
	makeTitleBar(W, panel, pad)

	-- Header content sits inside the panel padding, so controls keep their offsets from its edges.
	local header = Instance.new("Frame")
	header.Name = "Header"
	header.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	header.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, -pad)
	header.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, LAYOUT.TitleBar)
	header.Parent = panel

	local title = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	title.Name = "Title"
	title.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	title.Text = "Properties"
	title.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	title.Size = UDim2.new(1, -100, 1, 0)
	TypeScale.style(title, "Title")
	W.paint(title, "TextColor3", "TextPrimary")
	title.Parent = header

	local closeButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
	closeButton.Name = "Close"
	closeButton.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	closeButton.Text = "\u{00D7}"
	closeButton.Size = UDim2.new(0, 20, 1, 0)
	closeButton.Position = UDim2.new(1, -20, 0, 0)
	closeButton.ZIndex = 3
	TypeScale.style(closeButton, "Glyph")
	W.paint(closeButton, "TextColor3", "TextSecondary")
	closeButton.Parent = header
	makeDragHandle(W, panel, header)

	-- Search, then the list: each starts one panel padding below the element above it.
	local searchTop = LAYOUT.TitleBar
	local listTop = searchTop + LAYOUT.Search + pad
	local searchWrap = W.makeBlob("SearchWrap", panel, UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, LAYOUT.Search))
	searchWrap.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, searchTop)
	local searchBox = makeSearchBox(W, searchWrap, LAYOUT.FieldPad)
	TypeScale.style(searchBox, "Value")

	local scroll = makeScroll(W, panel, listTop, SCROLLBAR, LAYOUT.TypeGap)
	-- The list reaches into the panel's right padding by the gap plus the scrollbar and always
	-- reserves the bar's strip: rows stay as wide as the search field, stand clear of the bar,
	-- and a field's right outline is inside the list instead of on its clipping edge.
	scroll.Size = UDim2.new(1, SCROLLBAR_GAP + SCROLLBAR, 1, -listTop)
	scroll.VerticalScrollBarInset = Enum.ScrollBarInset.Always
	W.addPadding(scroll, 0, SCROLLBAR_GAP, 0, 0)

	return {
		header = header,
		closeButton = closeButton,
		searchWrap = searchWrap,
		searchBox = searchBox,
		scroll = scroll,
		top = searchTop,
		collapsedHeight = LAYOUT.TitleBar,
		arrowPosition = UDim2.new(1, -28, 0, 0),
		scrollbar = { thickness = SCROLLBAR, gap = SCROLLBAR_GAP },
	}
end

function PropertiesShell.build(W, panel)
	if C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
		return buildClassic(W, panel)
	end
	return buildModern(W, panel)
end

return PropertiesShell

--[[
	PropertiesTabs  -  the Properties panel's second view: one section at a time under tabs.

	The list view stays as it is. A button in the panel header switches between the two:
	  List   the scrolling list of type sections (search box included)
	  Tabs   the sections of one type as chips (wrapping onto further lines when they do not
	         fit) with the chosen section alone underneath, the full width of the panel.
	         Switching slides the section in from the side, as a tool deck's pages do. Two
	         arrows in the panel header step to the previous / next section and on into the
	         neighbouring type, and past the last one round to the first; turning the mouse
	         wheel over the chips or the arrows does the same. The wheel over the section
	         behaves as usual. The panel grows to hold a taller section and never shrinks by
	         itself, up to the panel's default height; a taller section scrolls. With several
	         types selected, a row of type chips sits above.

	PropertiesTabs.create(W, panel, parts) -> tabs
	  parts = { header, searchWrap, searchBox, scroll, top, scrollbar }   top = y of the area under
	      the header; scrollbar = { thickness, gap } from PropertiesShell (nil in Classic)
	  tabs.CollapseProbe      add it LAST to the header arrow's item list: the arrow hides and
	                          shows it with the list, which is how this view follows a collapse
	  tabs.Host               the ScrollingFrame the pages sit in
	  tabs.attach()           call once every type section exists under `scroll`
	  tabs.bindStore(plugin)  restores the saved view, then persists changes
	  tabs.setMode("list" | "tabs")

	Type sections are the children of `scroll` built by W.makeSection (`Header/Title` + `Body`).
	Mutates LIVE list frames through Pages alone (adopt reparents them and opens their Body,
	release undoes both); a type is adopted the first time it is opened. The list's own
	Visible flags (set by SelectionHandler) decide which types and sections get a chip.
	Mutates panel.Size while in Tabs (grow only; the user's own resize is kept when the open
	section fits it); the list's height is put back on return to List. A panel pushed by one
	in front (PanelPush) is not grown: its page scrolls until the push ends.
	Refreshed by: a type or section Visible / Title changing, the open section resizing, the
	panel resizing, theme changes.
	Cross-file invariant: W.makeDropdown switches off its ScrollingFrame ancestor's
	ScrollingEnabled while the cursor rests on it. Host is that ancestor here, and every page
	change switches it back on, because a dropdown can leave with its page.
	Plugin setting: PropsViewMode.
]]

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local ChipRow = require(script.ChipRow)
local Pages = require(script.Pages)
local T = C.T

local PropertiesTabs = {}

-- Between the type chips and the section chips.
local ROW_GAP = 8
-- Between the chips and the page; the divider runs through its middle. Classic has no divider
-- and keeps its tighter gap.
local PAGE_GAP = 12
local CLASSIC_PAGE_GAP = 4
-- Air under the page's last row.
local PAGE_BOTTOM = 4
local MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT = 40
local SCREEN_MARGIN = 8
-- The panel grows for a taller section up to this height (the panel's default); past it the
-- section scrolls. A taller manual resize is kept.
local MAX_GROWN_HEIGHT = C.LAYOUT.PropsHeight
-- The header's step arrows: width of each, and where the first sits from the header's right
-- edge (left of the view button).
local ARROW_WIDTH = 18
local ARROWS_RIGHT = 100
local ARROW_DIMMED = 0.65
-- Chips roomier than a tool deck's, by the theme's row height. Classic keeps the deck's.
local CHIP_PADDING = 16
local CHIP_GAP = 6
local WHEEL_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 0.12
local MODE_SETTING = "PropsViewMode"
-- QOLSearch restores the list 0.05 s after the search text changes; adoption waits for it.
local SEARCH_SETTLE_SECONDS = 0.12

local function contains(guiObject, point)
	local origin = guiObject.AbsolutePosition
	local size = guiObject.AbsoluteSize
	return point.X >= origin.X and point.Y >= origin.Y and point.X <= origin.X + size.X and point.Y <= origin.Y + size.Y
end

function PropertiesTabs.create(W, panel, parts)
	-- The panel's UIPadding, both edges together (BuildProperties sets it from LAYOUT.PanelPad).
	local PANEL_PADDING = C.LAYOUT.PanelPad * 2
	local scroll = parts.scroll
	local mode = "list"
	local collapsed = false
	local switching = false
	local store = nil
	local types = {}
	local typesByKey = {}
	local activeType = nil
	local listHeight = panel.Size.Y.Offset
	local pageHeight = MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT
	local chipsBottom = 0
	-- How much of the open page the screen leaves no room for (view units); 0 when it fits.
	-- Above 1 the page scrolls inside the host.
	local pageOverflow = 0
	-- The panel height in force. Opening a section may raise it, never lower it.
	local heldHeight = 0
	local sizeTween = nil
	local settingSize = false
	local lastWheel = 0

	local area = Instance.new("Frame")
	area.Name = "TabsView"
	area.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	area.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, parts.top)
	area.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -parts.top)
	area.Visible = false
	area.Parent = panel

	-- A ScrollingFrame so a section taller than the screen can still be reached, and so
	-- dropdowns find the ancestor they switch off.
	local host = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
	host.Name = "Pages"
	host.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	host.BorderSizePixel = 0
	host.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	host.ScrollingDirection = Enum.ScrollingDirection.Y
	host.ScrollBarThickness = 3
	host.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
	host.Parent = area
	table.insert(W.getThemed().scrollbars, host)
	-- As the list does (PropertiesShell): the host reaches into the panel's right padding by the
	-- gap plus the scrollbar, so a field's right outline is not on the host's clipping edge.
	local hostReach = 0
	if parts.scrollbar then
		hostReach = parts.scrollbar.gap + parts.scrollbar.thickness
		host.ScrollBarThickness = parts.scrollbar.thickness
		host.VerticalScrollBarInset = Enum.ScrollBarInset.Always
		W.addPadding(host, 0, parts.scrollbar.gap, 0, 0)
	end

	-- Hairline between the chips and the page.
	local divider = Instance.new("Frame")
	divider.Name = "Divider"
	divider.BorderSizePixel = 0
	divider.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1)
	divider.Visible = not C.MODE.Structure.Classic
	W.paint(divider, "BackgroundColor3", "Divider")
	divider.Parent = area
	local pageGap = C.MODE.Structure.Classic and CLASSIC_PAGE_GAP or PAGE_GAP

	-- The header's step arrows: click or wheel to step sections.
	local function makeArrow(name, glyph, fromRight)
		local arrow = Instance.new("TextButton")
		arrow.Name = name
		arrow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		arrow.AutoButtonColor = false
		arrow.Font = T.Font
		arrow.TextSize = 11
		arrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		arrow.Text = glyph
		-- Drawn like the header's collapse chevron beside them.
		if not C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
			TypeScale.style(arrow, "Chevron")
		end
		arrow.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
		arrow.Position = UDim2.new(1, -fromRight, 0, 0)
		arrow.Size = UDim2.new(0, ARROW_WIDTH, 1, 0)
		arrow.ZIndex = 3
		arrow.Visible = false
		arrow.Parent = parts.header
		arrow.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			if W.pointerBlocked(arrow) then return end
			arrow.TextColor3 = T.Gold
		end)
		arrow.MouseLeave:Connect(function() arrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold end)
		return arrow
	end
	local previousArrow = makeArrow("PreviousSection", "\u{2039}", ARROWS_RIGHT + ARROW_WIDTH)
	local nextArrow = makeArrow("NextSection", "\u{203A}", ARROWS_RIGHT)

	local probe = Instance.new("Frame")
	probe.Name = "CollapseProbe"
	probe.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	probe.Size = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	probe.Parent = panel

	local viewButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
	viewButton.Name = "ViewMode"
	viewButton.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	viewButton.Font = T.Font
	viewButton.TextSize = 9
	viewButton.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
	viewButton.Text = "List"
	viewButton.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
	viewButton.Position = UDim2.new(1, -54, 0, 0)
	viewButton.Size = UDim2.new(0, 44, 1, 0)
	viewButton.ZIndex = 3
	viewButton.Parent = parts.header

	local function screenScale()
		local screenGui = panel:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("ScreenGui")
		local uiScale = screenGui and screenGui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
		return uiScale and uiScale.Scale or 1
	end

	-- The tallest the panel may get: down to the bottom of the screen from where it sits.
	local function maxPanelHeight()
		local screenGui = panel:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("ScreenGui")
		if not screenGui then return math.huge end
		local scale = screenScale()
		local top = (panel.AbsolutePosition.Y - screenGui.AbsolutePosition.Y) / scale
		local room = screenGui.AbsoluteSize.Y / scale - top - SCREEN_MARGIN
		return math.max(room, PANEL_PADDING + parts.top + chipsBottom + MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT)
	end

	-- Grows the panel until it holds the chips plus the open page, up to MAX_GROWN_HEIGHT and the
	-- screen's bottom edge. Mutates panel.Size.
	local function applyHeight(animate)
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed then return end
		local wanted = PANEL_PADDING + parts.top + chipsBottom + pageHeight + PAGE_BOTTOM
		local limit = math.min(maxPanelHeight(), MAX_GROWN_HEIGHT)
		-- A panel pushed by one in front (PanelPush) keeps the height it was pushed to.
		local pushed = W.panelPushed(panel)
		if not pushed then heldHeight = math.max(heldHeight, math.min(wanted, limit)) end
		-- The page scrolls when the panel cannot hold it; otherwise the panel fits it.
		pageOverflow = math.max(0, wanted - heldHeight)
		local canvasHeight = 0
		if pageOverflow > 1 then canvasHeight = pageHeight end
		host.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, canvasHeight)
		if pushed then return end
		local size = UDim2.new(0, panel.Size.X.Offset, 0, heldHeight)

		local running = sizeTween
		sizeTween = nil
		if running then running:Cancel() end

		settingSize = true
		if animate and panel.Visible then
			local tween = TweenService:Create(panel, W.DeckSlide, { Size = size })
			sizeTween = tween
			tween.Completed:Connect(function()
				if sizeTween ~= tween then return end
				sizeTween = nil
				settingSize = false
			end)
			tween:Play()
		else
			panel.Size = size
			settingSize = false
		end
	end

	local typeRow
	local sectionRow

	local refreshArrows

	-- Stacks the chip rows, the divider and the page host for the panel's width, then resizes
	-- the panel.
	local function relayout(animate)
		local width = panel.Size.X.Offset - PANEL_PADDING
		local y = 0
		if typeRow.frame.Visible then
			typeRow.frame.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
			y = typeRow:layout(width) + ROW_GAP
		end
		sectionRow.frame.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, y)
		y += sectionRow:layout(width)
		divider.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, y + pageGap / 2)
		y += pageGap
		chipsBottom = y
		host.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, y)
		host.Size = UDim2.new(1, hostReach, 1, -y)
		refreshArrows()
		applyHeight(animate)
	end

	local pages
	local refreshSections

	pages = Pages.new(W, host, {
		onHeight = function(height)
			pageHeight = height
			applyHeight(true)
		end,
		onShownChanged = function(typeKey)
			if mode == "tabs" and activeType and activeType.key == typeKey then refreshSections() end
		end,
	})

	-- Pages are ordered by type, then by section, which gives a slide its direction.
	local function rankOf(page)
		return typesByKey[page.typeKey].rank * 1000 + page.index
	end

	-- stepDirection (optional) is the way a step is travelling: a step that wraps round keeps
	-- sliding that way instead of following the page order.
	local function openPage(page, animate, stepDirection)
		local direction = 1
		local current = pages.active
		if page and current and rankOf(page) < rankOf(current) then direction = -1 end
		if stepDirection then direction = stepDirection end
		host.CanvasPosition = Vector2.new(0, 0)
		-- A dropdown that left with its page never saw the cursor leave it.
		host.ScrollingEnabled = true
		pages:open(page, direction, animate)
		refreshArrows()
		if page then
			typesByKey[page.typeKey].lastKey = page.key
			sectionRow:setActive(page.key)
			return
		end
		sectionRow:setActive(nil)
		pageHeight = MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT
		applyHeight(animate)
	end

	local function shownTypes()
		local shown = {}
		for _, entry in ipairs(types) do
			if entry.frame.Visible then table.insert(shown, entry) end
		end
		return shown
	end

	-- Fills the section chips for the active type. Returns its shown pages.
	local function fillSectionChips()
		local shown = {}
		if activeType then shown = pages:shown(activeType.key) end
		local chips = {}
		for _, page in ipairs(shown) do
			table.insert(chips, { key = page.key, text = page.title })
		end
		sectionRow:setChips(chips)
		return shown
	end

	-- A section of the active type was shown or hidden: the chips follow, and the open page
	-- changes only when it is the one that went away.
	function refreshSections()
		local shown = fillSectionChips()
		local current = pages.active
		if current and table.find(shown, current) then
			sectionRow:setActive(current.key)
		else
			openPage(shown[1], false)
		end
		relayout(false)
	end

	-- Opens `entry`'s sections, adopting them on first use. which: "remembered" returns to
	-- the section last open in that type, "first" / "last" pick an end.
	local function openType(entry, which, animate, stepDirection)
		activeType = entry
		if not entry then
			typeRow:setActive(nil)
			fillSectionChips()
			openPage(nil, false)
			relayout(false)
			return
		end
		typeRow:setActive(entry.key)
		pages:adopt(entry.key, entry.body)
		local shown = fillSectionChips()
		local target = shown[1]
		if which == "last" then
			target = shown[#shown]
		elseif which == "remembered" then
			for _, page in ipairs(shown) do
				if page.key == entry.lastKey then target = page end
			end
		end
		openPage(target, animate, stepDirection)
		relayout(animate)
	end

	local function refreshTypes()
		local shown = shownTypes()
		local chips = {}
		for _, entry in ipairs(shown) do
			table.insert(chips, { key = entry.key, text = entry.title.Text })
		end
		typeRow:setChips(chips)
		typeRow.frame.Visible = #shown > 1
		if mode ~= "tabs" then return end
		if not activeType or not activeType.frame.Visible then
			openType(shown[1], "remembered", false)
		else
			typeRow:setActive(activeType.key)
			relayout(false)
		end
	end

	-- What lies `step` away from the open page: a page of the active type, or else the
	-- neighbouring type to carry on into. Either end wraps round to the other; nil, nil only
	-- when there is nowhere else to go.
	local function neighbourOf(step)
		if not activeType then return nil, nil end
		local shown = pages:shown(activeType.key)
		local index = table.find(shown, pages.active) or 0
		local page = shown[index + step]
		if page then return page, nil end

		local shownList = shownTypes()
		local typeAt = table.find(shownList, activeType)
		if typeAt and #shownList > 1 then
			return nil, shownList[(typeAt + step - 1) % #shownList + 1]
		end

		if #shown < 2 then return nil, nil end
		if step > 0 then return shown[1], nil end
		return shown[#shown], nil
	end

	local function stepSection(step)
		local page, entry = neighbourOf(step)
		if page then
			openPage(page, true, step)
		elseif entry and step > 0 then
			openType(entry, "first", true, step)
		elseif entry then
			openType(entry, "last", true, step)
		end
	end

	-- Dims an arrow that has nowhere to go.
	function refreshArrows()
		local previousPage, previousType = neighbourOf(-1)
		local nextPage, nextType = neighbourOf(1)
		previousArrow.TextTransparency = (previousPage or previousType) and 0 or ARROW_DIMMED
		nextArrow.TextTransparency = (nextPage or nextType) and 0 or ARROW_DIMMED
	end

	local chipMetrics = nil
	if not C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
		chipMetrics = { Height = C.LAYOUT.Row - 4, Padding = CHIP_PADDING, Gap = CHIP_GAP, Justify = true }
	end
	typeRow = ChipRow.new(W, area, function(key)
		local entry = typesByKey[key]
		if entry and entry ~= activeType then openType(entry, "remembered", true) end
	end, chipMetrics)
	typeRow.frame.Name = "TypeChips"
	typeRow.frame.Visible = false
	sectionRow = ChipRow.new(W, area, function(key)
		if not activeType then return end
		for _, page in ipairs(pages:shown(activeType.key)) do
			if page.key == key then openPage(page, true) end
		end
	end, chipMetrics)
	sectionRow.frame.Name = "SectionChips"

	local function applyVisibility()
		area.Visible = mode == "tabs" and not collapsed
		viewButton.Visible = not collapsed
		previousArrow.Visible = area.Visible
		nextArrow.Visible = area.Visible
		if mode == "tabs" then
			scroll.Visible = false
			parts.searchWrap.Visible = false
		elseif not collapsed then
			scroll.Visible = true
			parts.searchWrap.Visible = true
		end
		viewButton.Text = mode == "tabs" and "Tabs" or "List"
	end

	-- True when another top-level frame of the ScreenGui is drawn over the panel at `point`
	-- (a floating editor, an open dropdown list): the wheel belongs to that one.
	local function coveredAt(point)
		local screenGui = panel.Parent
		if not screenGui then return false end
		local pastPanel = false
		for _, sibling in ipairs(screenGui:GetChildren()) do
			if sibling == panel then
				pastPanel = true
			elseif sibling:IsA("GuiObject") and sibling.Visible then
				local above = sibling.ZIndex > panel.ZIndex or (sibling.ZIndex == panel.ZIndex and pastPanel)
				if above and contains(sibling, point) then return true end
			end
		end
		return false
	end

	local tabs = {}

	function tabs.setMode(nextMode)
		if nextMode == mode or collapsed or switching then return end
		switching = true
		if nextMode == "tabs" then
			if parts.searchBox.Text ~= "" then
				parts.searchBox.Text = ""
				task.wait(SEARCH_SETTLE_SECONDS)
			end
			listHeight = W.restingSize(panel).Y.Offset
			heldHeight = 0
			mode = "tabs"
			applyVisibility()
			activeType = nil
			refreshTypes()
		else
			mode = "list"
			pages:release()
			activeType = nil
			applyVisibility()
			local running = sizeTween
			sizeTween = nil
			if running then running:Cancel() end
			settingSize = false
			panel.Size = UDim2.new(0, panel.Size.X.Offset, 0, listHeight)
		end
		switching = false
		if store then pcall(function() store:SetSetting(MODE_SETTING, mode) end) end
	end

	function tabs.attach()
		for _, frame in ipairs(scroll:GetChildren()) do
			local header = frame:IsA("Frame") and frame:FindFirstChild("Header")
			local title = header and header:FindFirstChild("Title")
			local body = frame:FindFirstChild("Body")
			if title and body then
				-- lastKey: the section last open in this type. rank: its place in type order.
				local entry = { key = frame.Name, frame = frame, body = body, title = title, lastKey = nil, rank = 0 }
				table.insert(types, entry)
				typesByKey[entry.key] = entry
				frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(refreshTypes)
				title:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(refreshTypes)
			end
		end
		table.sort(types, function(a, b) return a.frame.LayoutOrder < b.frame.LayoutOrder end)
		for index, entry in ipairs(types) do
			entry.rank = index
		end
		refreshTypes()
	end

	function tabs.bindStore(pluginRef)
		store = pluginRef
		local okMode, savedMode = pcall(function() return pluginRef:GetSetting(MODE_SETTING) end)
		if okMode and savedMode == "tabs" then task.defer(tabs.setMode, "tabs") end
	end

	viewButton.Activated:Connect(function()
		tabs.setMode(mode == "tabs" and "list" or "tabs")
	end)
	previousArrow.Activated:Connect(function() stepSection(-1) end)
	nextArrow.Activated:Connect(function() stepSection(1) end)

	-- The header arrow hides / shows the probe together with the list.
	probe:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
		collapsed = not probe.Visible
		applyVisibility()
	end)

	-- A resize from outside (edge drag, Reset Layout, the header arrow) re-wraps the chips.
	-- Its height becomes the one held, raised again if the open page needs more.
	panel:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Size"):Connect(function()
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed or settingSize then return end
		heldHeight = panel.Size.Y.Offset
		relayout(false)
	end)

	table.insert(W.getUISConnections(), UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(input)
		if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel then return end
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed or not panel.Visible or not activeType then return end
		-- Only over the chips or the header arrows: the wheel over the page keeps its usual
		-- meaning (scrolling a tall section, cycling a dropdown).
		local mouse = UserInputService:GetMouseLocation()
		local overChips = contains(sectionRow.frame, mouse) or (typeRow.frame.Visible and contains(typeRow.frame, mouse))
		if not overChips and not contains(previousArrow, mouse) and not contains(nextArrow, mouse) then return end
		if coveredAt(mouse) then return end
		local now = os.clock()
		if now - lastWheel < WHEEL_COOLDOWN_SECONDS then return end
		lastWheel = now
		if input.Position.Z < 0 then
			stepSection(1)
		else
			stepSection(-1)
		end
	end))

	table.insert(W.getThemed().repaints, function()
		viewButton.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		previousArrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		nextArrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		typeRow:repaint()
		sectionRow:repaint()
		if mode == "tabs" and not collapsed then relayout(false) end
	end)

	tabs.CollapseProbe = probe
	tabs.Host = host
	return tabs
end

return PropertiesTabs

--[[
	ChipRow  -  a strip of the tool deck's tab chips that wraps onto further lines.

	The chips are placed by hand from measured text widths, so the strip's height is known the
	moment it is laid out: the Properties tabs size the panel from it in the same step.

	ChipRow.new(W, parent, onPick, metrics) -> row
	  metrics                    optional { Height, Padding, Gap, Justify } in place of the deck's
	                             W.chipMetrics(). Justify stretches every line but the last to
	                             the full width, so the lines share one left and right edge.
	  .frame                     the strip; the owner positions it, :layout sets its height
	  :setChips(list)            list = { { key = , text = }, ... } in display order
	  :setActive(key)            lights that chip
	  :layout(width) -> height   places the chips in lines no wider than `width` (view units)
	  :repaint()                 theme colours
	onPick(key) runs when a chip is clicked.

	Chips are W.makeChip buttons (WidgetDeck). They are reused and never destroyed, because
	makeChip registers each chip's stroke with the themed list for the life of the UI.
]]

local ChipRow = {}
ChipRow.__index = ChipRow

function ChipRow.new(W, parent, onPick, metrics)
	local self = setmetatable({}, ChipRow)

	local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
	frame.Name = "Chips"
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
	frame.Parent = parent

	self.frame = frame
	self._W = W
	self._metrics = metrics
	self._onPick = onPick
	self._buttons = {}
	self._chips = {}
	self._activeKey = nil
	return self
end

function ChipRow:_button(index)
	local button = self._buttons[index]
	if button then return button end
	button = self._W.makeChip("Chip" .. index, self.frame, "")
	button.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None
	if self._metrics then
		-- makeChip rounded the chip for the deck's height.
		local corner = button:FindFirstChildOfClass("UICorner")
		if corner then
			corner.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, self._metrics.Height / 2)
		end
	end
	button.Activated:Connect(function()
		local chip = self._chips[index]
		if chip then self._onPick(chip.key) end
	end)
	self._buttons[index] = button
	return button
end

function ChipRow:setChips(list)
	self._chips = list
	for index, chip in ipairs(list) do
		local button = self:_button(index)
		button.Text = chip.text
		button.Visible = true
	end
	for index = #list + 1, #self._buttons do
		self._buttons[index].Visible = false
	end
	self:repaint()
end

function ChipRow:setActive(key)
	self._activeKey = key
	self:repaint()
end

function ChipRow:repaint()
	for index, chip in ipairs(self._chips) do
		self._W.paintChip(self._buttons[index], chip.key == self._activeKey)
	end
end

function ChipRow:layout(width)
	local metrics = self._metrics or self._W.chipMetrics()

	-- Chips at their text's width, broken into lines no wider than `width`.
	local lines = {}
	local line = { used = 0 }
	for index, chip in ipairs(self._chips) do
		local button = self._buttons[index]
		local textWidth = self._W.chipTextWidth(button, chip.text)
		local chipWidth = math.min(math.ceil(textWidth) + metrics.Padding, width)
		if #line > 0 and line.used + metrics.Gap + chipWidth > width then
			table.insert(lines, line)
			line = { used = 0 }
		end
		if #line > 0 then
			line.used += metrics.Gap
		end
		table.insert(line, { button = button, width = chipWidth })
		line.used += chipWidth
	end
	if #line > 0 then
		table.insert(lines, line)
	end

	local y = 0
	for lineIndex, entries in ipairs(lines) do
		local spare = 0
		if metrics.Justify and lineIndex < #lines then
			spare = (width - entries.used) / #entries
		end
		local x = 0
		for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
			local left = math.floor(x + 0.5)
			local right = math.floor(x + entry.width + spare + 0.5)
			entry.button.Position = UDim2.new(0, left, 0, y)
			entry.button.Size = UDim2.new(0, right - left, 0, metrics.Height)
			x += entry.width + spare + metrics.Gap
		end
		y += metrics.Height + metrics.Gap
	end

	local height = 0
	if #lines > 0 then height = y - metrics.Gap end
	self.frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, height)
	return height
end

return ChipRow

--[[
	Pages  -  the section pages of the Properties tabs view.

	Each child of a type's list Body (its sections, plus blocks such as the Blender box) rides
	in a `Page` holder under the host, and one page shows at a time, sliding in from the side
	as a tool deck's pages do. The section frames are the LIVE ones the list uses: adopt()
	takes them out of their Body and release() puts them back, so every ref in UI.<Type> keeps
	working in both views.

	A section does not collapse here: adopt() opens its Body and hides the header's Arrow and
	Toggle, release() restores all three. The list's stored collapse state is not touched.

	Pages.new(W, host, callbacks) -> pages
	  callbacks.onHeight(height)          the open page's height in view units: on open when it
	                                      is already known, and whenever it is measured anew
	  callbacks.onShownChanged(typeKey)   the list's owner showed or hid a section of that type
	  .active                             the open page or nil (read only)
	  :adopt(typeKey, body)               no-op for a type that is already adopted
	  :release()
	  :shown(typeKey) -> { page, ... }    pages whose section is visible, in section order
	  :open(page, direction, animate)     direction 1 slides in from the right, -1 from the left;
	                                      page nil closes the open page
	  page = { typeKey, key, title, index, ... }   index = place among its type's pages

	Cross-file invariant: a frame with `Header/Toggle` and `Body` is a W.makeSection section.
]]

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Pages = {}
Pages.__index = Pages

local ORIGIN = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)

-- Arrow, Body and Toggle of a W.makeSection section; nil for any other frame.
local function sectionParts(frame)
	local header = frame:FindFirstChild("Header")
	local body = frame:FindFirstChild("Body")
	local toggle = header and header:FindFirstChild("Toggle")
	if not body or not toggle then return nil, nil, nil end
	return header:FindFirstChild("Arrow"), body, toggle
end

-- The name a page takes from its section.
local function titleOf(frame)
	local header = frame:FindFirstChild("Header")
	local title = header and header:FindFirstChild("Title")
	if title and title:IsA("TextLabel") then return title.Text end
	local label = frame:FindFirstChild("Label", true)
	if label and label:IsA("TextLabel") then return label.Text end
	return frame.Name
end

function Pages.new(W, host, callbacks)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Pages)
	self._W = W
	self._host = host
	self._callbacks = callbacks
	self._types = {}
	self._slides = {}
	self.active = nil
	return self
end

function Pages:_screenScale()
	local screenGui = self._host:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("ScreenGui")
	local uiScale = screenGui and screenGui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
	return uiScale and uiScale.Scale or 1
end

-- Reads the open page's height. A hidden page is not measured: its layout may be stale.
function Pages:_measure(page)
	if page ~= self.active then return end
	local height = page.frame.AbsoluteSize.Y / self:_screenScale()
	if height < 1 then return end
	if page.height and math.abs(height - page.height) < 0.5 then return end
	page.height = height
	self._callbacks.onHeight(height)
end

function Pages:_makePage(typeKey, frame)
	local holder = Instance.new("Frame")
	holder.Name = "Page"
	holder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	holder.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
	holder.Visible = false
	holder.Parent = self._host

	local arrow, body, toggle = sectionParts(frame)
	local page = {
		typeKey = typeKey,
		key = frame.Name,
		title = titleOf(frame),
		index = 0,
		frame = frame,
		holder = holder,
		arrow = arrow,
		body = body,
		toggle = toggle,
		bodyWasOpen = body ~= nil and body.Visible,
		height = nil,
		connections = {},
	}

	if body then
		body.Visible = true
		toggle.Visible = false
		if arrow then arrow.Visible = false end
	end
	frame.Parent = holder

	table.insert(page.connections, frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
		self._callbacks.onShownChanged(typeKey)
	end))
	table.insert(page.connections, frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(function()
		self:_measure(page)
	end))
	return page
end

-- Moves every GuiObject child of `body` (LIVE list frames) into a page holder.
function Pages:adopt(typeKey, body)
	if self._types[typeKey] then return end
	local entry = { body = body, pages = {} }
	self._types[typeKey] = entry
	for _, child in ipairs(body:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("GuiObject") then
			table.insert(entry.pages, self:_makePage(typeKey, child))
		end
	end
	table.sort(entry.pages, function(a, b) return a.frame.LayoutOrder < b.frame.LayoutOrder end)
	for index, page in ipairs(entry.pages) do
		page.index = index
	end
end

-- Returns every adopted frame to its list Body as it was, and drops the holders.
function Pages:release()
	self:_finishSlides()
	for _, entry in pairs(self._types) do
		for _, page in ipairs(entry.pages) do
			for _, connection in ipairs(page.connections) do
				connection:Disconnect()
			end
			if page.body then
				page.body.Visible = page.bodyWasOpen
				page.toggle.Visible = true
				if page.arrow then page.arrow.Visible = true end
			end
			page.frame.Parent = entry.body
			page.holder:Destroy()
		end
	end
	self._types = {}
	self.active = nil
end

function Pages:shown(typeKey)
	local shown = {}
	local entry = self._types[typeKey]
	if not entry then return shown end
	for _, page in ipairs(entry.pages) do
		if page.frame.Visible then table.insert(shown, page) end
	end
	return shown
end

-- Ends any slide still running: every holder is back at the origin and a page that was
-- leaving is hidden.
function Pages:_finishSlides()
	for _, slide in ipairs(self._slides) do
		slide.tween:Cancel()
		slide.holder.Position = ORIGIN
		if slide.leaving then slide.holder.Visible = false end
	end
	self._slides = {}
end

function Pages:_slide(holder, target, leaving)
	local tween = TweenService:Create(holder, self._W.DeckSlide, { Position = target })
	table.insert(self._slides, { tween = tween, holder = holder, leaving = leaving })
	if leaving then
		tween.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
			if playbackState ~= Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then return end
			holder.Visible = false
			holder.Position = ORIGIN
		end)
	end
	tween:Play()
end

function Pages:open(page, direction, animate)
	local outgoing = self.active
	if outgoing == page then return end
	self:_finishSlides()
	self.active = page

	local slides = animate and outgoing ~= nil and page ~= nil
	if outgoing then
		if slides then
			self:_slide(outgoing.holder, UDim2.new(-direction, 0, 0, 0), true)
		else
			outgoing.holder.Visible = false
		end
	end
	if not page then return end

	page.holder.Visible = true
	if slides then
		page.holder.Position = UDim2.new(direction, 0, 0, 0)
		self:_slide(page.holder, ORIGIN, false)
	else
		page.holder.Position = ORIGIN
	end

	if page.height then self._callbacks.onHeight(page.height) end
	-- The page lays out on the next frame; its AbsoluteSize signal stays silent when the
	-- size it had while hidden was already right, so the height is read once here as well.
	task.spawn(function()
		task.wait()
		self:_measure(page)
	end)
end

return Pages

--[[
	RandomizerPanel  -  Part-Icles V5 Randomizer System
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Modal panel scaffolding:
	  - panel frame with title + close button
	  - section list (populated by RandomizerWiring.populateSections)
	  - Roll / Apply / Cancel button row

	Layout:
	  [Randomize Panel  -  modal]
	  [tristate checkbox tree of randomizable properties + Group axes / palette toggles]
	  [Roll]   [Apply]   [Cancel]

	Snapshot-preview-apply flow (handled in RandomizerWiring):
	  Open  -> QOL.snapshotItem per item
	  Roll  -> per-item per-prop derive() + roll() + RandomizerWriter.write()
	  Apply -> ChangeHistory waypoint, drop snapshots
	  Cancel -> QOL.restoreSnapshots(snapshots), close
]]

local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local W = require(script.Parent.Widgets)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local PanelSizes = require(script.Parent.PanelSizes)
local T = C.T
local LAYOUT = C.LAYOUT

local RandomizerPanel = {}

-- Build the modal panel frame. Returns refs map: {panel, sectionList, rollAllBtn,
-- applyBtn, cancelBtn, headerCloseBtn}. headerCloseBtn is W.makeToolPanel's built-in
-- `Hd.Close` (re-exposed here so wiring can attach a Cancel handler  -  every close
-- path must route through wiring.cancel() to restore preview snapshots). Caller
-- wires the buttons via the RandomizerWiring companion module.
local function buildClassic(sg)
	-- Modal panel ~ same dimensions as InventoryPanel for visual consistency. _opaquePanel
	-- so it stays opaque when global panel translucency is set; _noSnap so it doesn't
	-- participate in resolveOverlap (modal-positioned in front of Properties panel).
	-- 220px width: rows are simple (label blob + toggle); 220 fits the longest prop
	-- names (e.g. "AccelerationTowardsInstance") with truncation as fallback.
	local panel = W.makeToolPanel(sg, "Randomize", 220, 400)
	panel:SetAttribute("_opaquePanel", true)
	panel:SetAttribute("_noSnap", true)
	panel.Visible = false  -- toolbar toggle controls visibility

	local refs = {panel = panel}

	-- W.makeToolPanel already installs an `Hd.Close` button that hides the panel via
	-- `panel.Visible = false`. We expose it as `headerCloseBtn` so the wiring layer
	-- can attach its own Cancel handler  -  ALL close paths must route through
	-- wiring.cancel() to restore preview snapshots.
	local hd = panel:FindFirstChild("Hd")
	if hd then refs.headerCloseBtn = hd:FindFirstChild("Close") end

	-- Section list (scrolling). Populated by RandomizerWiring.populateSections.
	local sectionList = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
	sectionList.Name = "SectionList"
	sectionList.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	sectionList.BorderSizePixel = 0
	sectionList.Position = UDim2.new(0, 4, 0, 26)
	sectionList.Size = UDim2.new(1, -8, 1, -56)
	sectionList.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	sectionList.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	sectionList.ScrollBarThickness = 2
	sectionList.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
	sectionList.Parent = panel
	W.addListLayout(sectionList, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)
	refs.sectionList = sectionList

	-- Placeholder shown only until RandomizerWiring.populateSections rebuilds the list
	-- (which destroys all TextLabel/Frame children of sectionList).
	local placeholder = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	placeholder.Name = "Placeholder"
	placeholder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	placeholder.Text = "Loading…"
	placeholder.TextColor3 = T.DarkGold
	placeholder.Font = T.Font
	placeholder.TextSize = 8
	placeholder.TextWrapped = true
	placeholder.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Center
	placeholder.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 32)
	placeholder.Parent = sectionList

	-- Three buttons evenly across the row.
	local btnRow = Instance.new("Frame")
	btnRow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	btnRow.Size = UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22)
	btnRow.Position = UDim2.new(0, 4, 1, -26)
	btnRow.Parent = panel
	W.addListLayout(btnRow, 2, Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal)

	refs.rollAllBtn = W.makeButton("RandRoll", btnRow, "Roll", UDim2.new(1/3, -2, 1, 0))
	refs.rollAllBtn.LayoutOrder = 0
	refs.rollAllBtn.TextSize = 9
	refs.applyBtn = W.makeButton("RandApply", btnRow, "Apply", UDim2.new(1/3, -2, 1, 0), T.Gold)
	refs.applyBtn.LayoutOrder = 1
	refs.applyBtn.TextSize = 9
	refs.cancelBtn = W.makeButton("RandCancel", btnRow, "Cancel", UDim2.new(1/3, -2, 1, 0), T.DarkGold)
	refs.cancelBtn.LayoutOrder = 2
	refs.cancelBtn.TextSize = 9

	return refs
end

-- The same refs on the mode's tool shell: the list fills the body, the buttons sit under it.
local function buildModern(sg)
	local sizes = PanelSizes.get()
	local panel, chrome = W.makeToolShell(sg, "Randomize", sizes.Randomizer, sizes.RandomizerHeight)
	panel:SetAttribute("_opaquePanel", true)
	panel:SetAttribute("_noSnap", true)
	local body = chrome.body

	-- Every close path must reach wiring.cancel(), which restores the previewed values.
	local refs = { panel = panel, headerCloseBtn = chrome.close }

	-- RandomizerWiring.populateSections fills the list.
	local sectionList = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
	sectionList.Name = "SectionList"
	sectionList.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	sectionList.BorderSizePixel = 0
	sectionList.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -(LAYOUT.Row + LAYOUT.RowGap))
	sectionList.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	sectionList.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	sectionList.ScrollBarThickness = 4
	sectionList.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
	sectionList.Parent = body
	W.addListLayout(sectionList, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)
	table.insert(W.getThemed().scrollbars, sectionList)
	refs.sectionList = sectionList

	-- Shown until populateSections rebuilds the list.
	local placeholder = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	placeholder.Name = "Placeholder"
	placeholder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	placeholder.Text = "Loading…"
	placeholder.TextWrapped = true

--[[
	ThemeApply  -  live theme changes: UpdateTheme, SnapshotTheme, RestoreTheme.
	Loaded by UIBuilder/init.luau; receives UIBuilder and the Widgets table and adds the three
	methods to UIBuilder.
	UpdateTheme takes the saved theme values (nil = unchanged), recomputes every derived colour
	through Constants.refresh(), then repaints in two steps. First a walk moves text and frames
	that no registry knows, told only by their carrying an old role colour, onto the new one.
	Then the registered instances are painted from their roles. The order matters: the walk
	goes by colour alone, and a new panel colour can equal an old text colour (a dark theme's
	text against a light theme's panels), so whatever it made of a registered instance is put
	right by the repaint after it.
	Image tints are never matched by colour: an image shows a texture, a thumbnail or a picker
	surface. An icon that follows the theme registers its own repaint (W.paint, or a function
	in the repaints list).
	A mode or text-size change is not handled here: it changes sizes, so the UI is rebuilt.
]]

local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local T = C.T

-- Roles the colour-matching walk follows, in priority order: when two roles share a colour
-- before a change, text carrying it follows the earlier role.
local TEXT_ROLES = { "TextPrimary", "TextHeading", "TextLabel", "TextSecondary", "TextDisabled", "Accent", "Success", "Warning", "Danger" }

-- Colours are stored at 8 bits; anything closer than half a step is the same colour.
local SAME_COLOR = 0.002

local function sameColor(first, second)
	return math.abs(first.R - second.R) < SAME_COLOR
		and math.abs(first.G - second.G) < SAME_COLOR
		and math.abs(first.B - second.B) < SAME_COLOR
end

-- Drops destroyed instances from a registry list. `key` names the instance field of table entries.
local function sweepDead(list, key)
	local kept = 1
	for index = 1, #list do
		local entry = list[index]
		local inst = key and entry[key] or entry
		if inst and inst.Parent then
			list[kept] = entry
			kept += 1
		end
	end
	for index = kept, #list do
		list[index] = nil
	end
end

-- { old, new } pairs for the text roles whose colour changed.
local function changedTextRoles(before)
	local remap = {}
	for _, role in ipairs(TEXT_ROLES) do
		local old = before[role]
		local claimed = false
		for _, pair in ipairs(remap) do
			if sameColor(pair.old, old) then
				claimed = true
				break
			end
		end
		if not claimed and not sameColor(old, T[role]) then
			table.insert(remap, { old = old, new = T[role] })
		end
	end
	return remap
end

local function remapColor(color, remap)
	for _, pair in ipairs(remap) do
		if sameColor(color, pair.old) then
			return pair.new
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Moves every text and accent-coloured frame from an old role colour to the new one.
-- Anything marked `_noColorRemap` is left alone: a user colour, a compositing layer, or white
-- text on a coloured fill. So is any frame under a UIGradient: its colour is the gradient's
-- base, never a theme colour.
local function remapDescendants(screenGui, remap)
	for _, desc in ipairs(screenGui:GetDescendants()) do
		if desc:GetAttribute("_noColorRemap") then
			continue
		end
		if desc:IsA("TextLabel") or desc:IsA("TextButton") or desc:IsA("TextBox") then
			local text = remapColor(desc.TextColor3, remap)
			if text then
				desc.TextColor3 = text
			end
			if desc:IsA("TextBox") then
				local placeholder = remapColor(desc.PlaceholderColor3, remap)
				if placeholder then
					desc.PlaceholderColor3 = placeholder
				end
			end
		elseif desc:IsA("Frame") or desc:IsA("ScrollingFrame") then
			local fill = remapColor(desc.BackgroundColor3, remap)
			if fill and not desc:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIGradient") then
				desc.BackgroundColor3 = fill
			end
		end
	end
end

return function(UIBuilder, W)
	-- Repaints everything the registries track from the current T.
	local function repaintRegistered(themed)
		for _, stroke in ipairs(themed.strokes) do
			stroke.Color = T.Border
			stroke.Transparency = T.BorderAlpha
		end
		for _, panel in ipairs(themed.panels) do
			panel.BackgroundColor3 = T.PanelBg
			-- Modal dialogs stay solid whatever the theme's see-through.
			if not panel:GetAttribute("_opaquePanel") then
				panel.BackgroundTransparency = T.PanelAlpha
			end
		end
		for _, blob in ipairs(themed.blobs) do
			blob.BackgroundColor3 = T.BlobBg
			blob.BackgroundTransparency = T.BlobAlpha
		end
		for _, fill in ipairs(themed.fills) do
			fill.BackgroundColor3 = T.SliderFill
		end
		for _, scrollbar in ipairs(themed.scrollbars) do
			scrollbar.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
		end
		for _, entry in ipairs(themed.roles) do
			entry.inst[entry.prop] = T[entry.role]
		end
		-- After strokes: a toggle's outline depends on its state.
		for _, toggle in ipairs(themed.toggles) do
			W.paintToggle(toggle)
		end

		-- Producer: WidgetAxis.trackAxis registers { btn, color, selBg }; `_selected` on the button
		-- (set by the axis-toggle handlers) picks the selected paint.
		for _, entry in ipairs(themed.axisButtons) do
			local button = entry.btn
			if button.Parent then
				W.paintAxisButton(button, entry.color, entry.selBg, button:GetAttribute("_selected") == true)
			end
		end
		for _, entry in ipairs(themed.axisColored) do
			if entry.inst and entry.inst.Parent then
				local color = T["Axis" .. (entry.axis or "X")]
				if color then
					entry.inst[entry.prop] = color
				end
			end
		end
		for _, dot in ipairs(themed.evenDots) do
			dot.BackgroundColor3 = dot:GetAttribute("_even") and T.BrightGold or T.DarkGold
		end
		for _, image in ipairs(themed.panelImages) do
			image.Image = T.BgImage or ""
			image.ImageTransparency = T.BgImageTransparency or 1
		end
		-- Widgets that paint from T themselves (deck tabs, tray chips, the workspace bar).
		for _, repaint in ipairs(themed.repaints) do
			pcall(repaint)
		end
	end

	-- panelAlpha and blobAlpha are saved with the theme and drawn by the Classic mode only.
	-- Argument 10 (font scale) is accepted and ignored: text sizes come from the theme's text size.
	function UIBuilder:UpdateTheme(accent, background, slider, panelAlpha, blobAlpha, fontName, textAccent, blobColor, scrollBarColor, _fontScale, bgImage, bgImageTransparency)
		local themed = W.getThemed()
		for _, name in ipairs({ "strokes", "panels", "blobs", "fills", "scrollbars", "toggles", "panelImages", "evenDots" }) do
			sweepDead(themed[name])
		end
		sweepDead(themed.roles, "inst")

		local before = {}
		for _, role in ipairs(TEXT_ROLES) do
			before[role] = T[role]
		end

		if accent then
			T.InputAccent = accent
		end
		if background then
			T.InputBg = background
		end
		if slider then
			T.InputSlider = slider
		end
		if blobColor then
			T.InputBlob = blobColor
		end
		if scrollBarColor then
			T.InputScrollBar = scrollBarColor
		end
		if textAccent then
			T.TextAccent = textAccent
		end
		if panelAlpha ~= nil then
			T.InputPanelAlpha = panelAlpha
		end
		if blobAlpha ~= nil then
			T.InputBlobAlpha = blobAlpha
		end
		if bgImage ~= nil then
			T.BgImage = bgImage
		end
		if bgImageTransparency ~= nil then
			T.BgImageTransparency = bgImageTransparency
		end

		local fontChanged = false
		if fontName and fontName ~= T.Font.Name then
			local ok, font = pcall(function()
				return Enum.Font[fontName]
			end)
			if ok and font then
				T.Font = font
				fontChanged = true
			end
		end

		C.refresh()

		-- Before the registered repaint, never after it: see the header.
		local screenGui = self._screenGui
		if screenGui then
			local remap = changedTextRoles(before)
			if #remap > 0 then
				remapDescendants(screenGui, remap)
			end
		end
		repaintRegistered(themed)
		if fontChanged and screenGui then
			TypeScale.reapply(screenGui)
		end
	end

	function UIBuilder:SnapshotTheme()
		return {
			Accent = T.InputAccent,
			Background = T.InputBg,
			Slider = T.InputSlider,
			Blob = T.InputBlob,
			ScrollBar = T.InputScrollBar,
			TextAccent = T.TextAccent,
			PanelAlpha = T.InputPanelAlpha,
			BlobAlpha = T.InputBlobAlpha,
			Font = T.Font,
			BgImage = T.BgImage,
			BgImageTransparency = T.BgImageTransparency,
		}
	end

	function UIBuilder:RestoreTheme(snapshot)
		self:UpdateTheme(snapshot.Accent, snapshot.Background, snapshot.Slider, snapshot.PanelAlpha, snapshot.BlobAlpha, snapshot.Font.Name,
			snapshot.TextAccent, snapshot.Blob, snapshot.ScrollBar, nil, snapshot.BgImage or "", snapshot.BgImageTransparency or 1)
	end
end

--[[
	ThemeModes  -  the selectable looks of the plugin UI: Typo, Slate, Shannon and Classic.
	API:
	  ThemeModes.ORDER, ThemeModes.DEFAULT, ThemeModes.TEXT_SIZES, ThemeModes.DEFAULT_TEXT_SIZE
	  ThemeModes.get(id)             mode table; an unknown id falls back to the default mode.
	  ThemeModes.textSize(value)     a supported text size; anything else falls back to the default.
	  ThemeModes.resolve(inputs, id, textSize)   { Id, Structure, Metrics, Surface, Roles }
	Inputs are the saved theme colours: { panel, field, accent, text, slider, scrollBar }.
	Roles are derived on every call and never saved, so the theme format stays the same.
	Consumer: UIBuilder/Constants fills T and LAYOUT from the result.
]]

local ColorMath = require(script.ColorMath)

local ThemeModes = {}

local MODES = {
	Typo = require(script.Typo),
	Slate = require(script.Slate),
	Shannon = require(script.Shannon),
	Classic = require(script.Classic),
}

ThemeModes.ColorMath = ColorMath
ThemeModes.ORDER = { "Typo", "Slate", "Shannon", "Classic" }
ThemeModes.DEFAULT = "Typo"
-- Only multiples of 4 draw on whole pixels at the 125% default UI scale.
ThemeModes.TEXT_SIZES = { 12, 16 }
ThemeModes.DEFAULT_TEXT_SIZE = 16

-- Status hues with the saturation each is solved at.
local STATUS = {
	Success = { color = Color3.fromRGB(139, 195, 74), saturation = 0.62 },
	Warning = { color = Color3.fromRGB(224, 160, 64), saturation = 0.70 },
	Danger = { color = Color3.fromRGB(238, 100, 100), saturation = 0.58 },
}
local STATUS_FLOOR = 4.6
local FILL_FLOOR = 3.1

function ThemeModes.get(id)
	return MODES[id] or MODES[ThemeModes.DEFAULT]
end

function ThemeModes.textSize(value)
	for _, size in ipairs(ThemeModes.TEXT_SIZES) do
		if size == value then
			return size
		end
	end
	return ThemeModes.DEFAULT_TEXT_SIZE
end

-- A saved fill colour is kept when it stands out from `background`, otherwise it is re-solved.
local function resolveFill(saved, background, light)
	if ColorMath.contrast(saved, background) >= FILL_FLOOR then
		return saved
	end
	local hue, saturation = saved:ToHSV()
	return ColorMath.solveTone(hue, saturation, { background }, FILL_FLOOR, light)
end

-- Roles the modes share unless a mode sets its own: status colours and the slider / scrollbar fills.
local function addSharedRoles(roles, inputs)
	local light = ColorMath.isLight(roles.Panel)
	local surfaces = { roles.Panel, roles.Field, roles.Header }
	for name, status in pairs(STATUS) do
		if roles[name] == nil then
			local hue = status.color:ToHSV()
			roles[name] = ColorMath.solveTone(hue, status.saturation, surfaces, STATUS_FLOOR, light)
		end
	end
	if roles.SliderFill == nil then
		roles.SliderFill = resolveFill(inputs.slider, roles.Field, light)
	end
	if roles.ScrollBar == nil then
		roles.ScrollBar = resolveFill(inputs.scrollBar, roles.Panel, light)
	end
end

function ThemeModes.resolve(inputs, id, textSize)
	local mode = ThemeModes.get(id)
	local roles = mode.derive(inputs, ColorMath)
	addSharedRoles(roles, inputs)
	return {
		Id = mode.Id,
		Structure = mode.Structure,
		Metrics = mode.Metrics[ThemeModes.textSize(textSize)],
		Surface = mode.Surface,
		Roles = roles,
	}
end

return ThemeModes

--[[
	ColorMath  -  contrast and colour-space helpers for theme derivation. Pure; no requires.
	API: quantize, luminance, contrast, minContrast, mix, isLight, toOklch, fromOklch,
	oklchWithContrast, solveTone, backOff.
	Contrast is the WCAG ratio (1 to 21). OKLCH keeps hue steady while lightness changes.
]]

local ColorMath = {}

local WHITE = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
local BLACK = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)

-- A panel brighter than this counts as a light theme.
local LIGHT_THEME_LUMINANCE = 0.18

local function channelToLinear(channel)
	if channel <= 0.04045 then
		return channel / 12.92
	end
	return ((channel + 0.055) / 1.055) ^ 2.4
end

local function linearToChannel(value)
	value = math.clamp(value, 0, 1)
	if value <= 0.0031308 then
		return 12.92 * value
	end
	return 1.055 * value ^ (1 / 2.4) - 0.055
end

-- Round each channel to 8 bits, the precision a saved theme keeps.
function ColorMath.quantize(color)
	local red = math.floor(color.R * 255 + 0.5)
	local green = math.floor(color.G * 255 + 0.5)
	local blue = math.floor(color.B * 255 + 0.5)
	return Color3.fromRGB(red, green, blue)
end

-- WCAG relative luminance, 0 to 1.
function ColorMath.luminance(color)
	return 0.2126 * channelToLinear(color.R) + 0.7152 * channelToLinear(color.G) + 0.0722 * channelToLinear(color.B)
end

-- WCAG contrast ratio between two colours.
function ColorMath.contrast(first, second)
	local firstLuminance = ColorMath.luminance(first)
	local secondLuminance = ColorMath.luminance(second)
	local brighter = math.max(firstLuminance, secondLuminance)
	local darker = math.min(firstLuminance, secondLuminance)
	return (brighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)
end

-- Lowest contrast of `color` against a list of backgrounds.
function ColorMath.minContrast(color, backgrounds)
	local lowest = math.huge
	for _, background in ipairs(backgrounds) do
		lowest = math.min(lowest, ColorMath.contrast(color, background))
	end
	return lowest
end

-- sRGB blend of `from` toward `to`, rounded to 8 bits.
function ColorMath.mix(from, to, amount)
	return ColorMath.quantize(from:Lerp(to, amount))
end

function ColorMath.isLight(color)
	return ColorMath.luminance(color) > LIGHT_THEME_LUMINANCE
end

-- Returns lightness (0 to 1), chroma and hue (degrees).
function ColorMath.toOklch(color)
	local red = channelToLinear(color.R)
	local green = channelToLinear(color.G)
	local blue = channelToLinear(color.B)

	local long = (0.4122214708 * red + 0.5363325363 * green + 0.0514459929 * blue) ^ (1 / 3)
	local medium = (0.2119034982 * red + 0.6806995451 * green + 0.1073969566 * blue) ^ (1 / 3)
	local short = (0.0883024619 * red + 0.2817188376 * green + 0.6299787005 * blue) ^ (1 / 3)

	local lightness = 0.2104542553 * long + 0.7936177850 * medium - 0.0040720468 * short
	local greenRed = 1.9779984951 * long - 2.4285922050 * medium + 0.4505937099 * short
	local blueYellow = 0.0259040371 * long + 0.7827717662 * medium - 0.8086757660 * short

	local chroma = math.sqrt(greenRed * greenRed + blueYellow * blueYellow)
	local hue = math.deg(math.atan2(blueYellow, greenRed)) % 360
	return lightness, chroma, hue
end

-- Linear sRGB channels for an OKLCH colour; values outside 0..1 are out of gamut.
local function oklchToLinear(lightness, chroma, hue)
	local greenRed = chroma * math.cos(math.rad(hue))
	local blueYellow = chroma * math.sin(math.rad(hue))

	local long = (lightness + 0.3963377774 * greenRed + 0.2158037573 * blueYellow) ^ 3
	local medium = (lightness - 0.1055613458 * greenRed - 0.0638541728 * blueYellow) ^ 3
	local short = (lightness - 0.0894841775 * greenRed - 1.2914855480 * blueYellow) ^ 3

	local red = 4.0767416621 * long - 3.3077115913 * medium + 0.2309699292 * short
	local green = -1.2684380046 * long + 2.6097574011 * medium - 0.3413193965 * short
	local blue = -0.0041960863 * long - 0.7034186147 * medium + 1.7076147010 * short
	return red, green, blue
end

local function inGamut(value)
	return value >= -0.0001 and value <= 1.0001
end

-- OKLCH to an 8-bit colour. Out-of-gamut colours lose chroma until they fit.
function ColorMath.fromOklch(lightness, chroma, hue)
	local reduced = chroma
	for _ = 1, 60 do
		local red, green, blue = oklchToLinear(lightness, reduced, hue)
		if inGamut(red) and inGamut(green) and inGamut(blue) then
			return ColorMath.quantize(Color3.new(linearToChannel(red), linearToChannel(green), linearToChannel(blue)))
		end
		reduced *= 0.95
	end
	local red, green, blue = oklchToLinear(lightness, 0, hue)
	return ColorMath.quantize(Color3.new(linearToChannel(red), linearToChannel(green), linearToChannel(blue)))
end

-- OKLCH colour whose lightness moves away from the backgrounds until `floor` contrast holds.
function ColorMath.oklchWithContrast(lightness, chroma, hue, backgrounds, floor, light)
	local step = light and -0.02 or 0.02
	local current = lightness
	local color = ColorMath.fromOklch(current, chroma, hue)
	while ColorMath.minContrast(color, backgrounds) < floor and current > 0.02 and current < 0.98 do
		current += step
		color = ColorMath.fromOklch(current, chroma, hue)
	end
	-- A mid-tone background can be out of reach for a tinted colour; plain black or white is the most it allows.
	if ColorMath.minContrast(color, backgrounds) < floor then
		return light and BLACK or WHITE
	end
	return color
end

-- True when `color` sits on the far side of every background and reaches `target` against each.
local function reaches(color, backgrounds, target, light)
	local colorLuminance = ColorMath.luminance(color)
	for _, background in ipairs(backgrounds) do
		local backgroundLuminance = ColorMath.luminance(background)
		if light and colorLuminance >= backgroundLuminance then
			return false
		end
		if not light and colorLuminance <= backgroundLuminance then
			return false
		end
		if ColorMath.contrast(color, background) < target then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

local function fromHsv(hue, saturation, value)
	return ColorMath.quantize(Color3.fromHSV(hue, saturation, value))
end

-- The least extreme HSV value that reaches `target` against every background at the given
-- hue. Saturation drops in steps of 0.05 when full value (or zero, for light themes) misses.
function ColorMath.solveTone(hue, saturation, backgrounds, target, light)
	local current = saturation
	while current >= -0.001 do
		local used = math.max(0, current)
		local extreme = light and 0 or 1
		if reaches(fromHsv(hue, used, extreme), backgrounds, target, light) then
			-- Bisection: 30 halvings resolve value far below 1/255.
			local low = 0
			local high = 1
			for _ = 1, 30 do
				local middle = (low + high) / 2
				local passes = reaches(fromHsv(hue, used, middle), backgrounds, target, light)
				if passes == light then
					low = middle
				else
					high = middle
				end
			end
			if light then
				return fromHsv(hue, used, low)
			end
			local value = high
			local color = fromHsv(hue, used, value)
			-- 8-bit rounding can land just under the target; step up until it holds.
			while not reaches(color, backgrounds, target, light) and value < 1 do
				value = math.min(1, value + 0.004)
				color = fromHsv(hue, used, value)
			end
			return color
		end
		current -= 0.05
	end
	return light and BLACK or WHITE
end

-- `from` pulled toward `to` by `pull`, easing back in steps of 0.01 until `floor` holds.
function ColorMath.backOff(from, to, pull, floor, backgrounds)
	local amount = pull
	while amount > 0 and ColorMath.minContrast(ColorMath.mix(from, to, amount), backgrounds) < floor do
		amount = math.floor((amount - 0.01) * 100 + 0.5) / 100
	end
	return ColorMath.mix(from, to, amount)
end

return ColorMath

--[[
	Shannon  -  theme mode with a calm, editorial look: warm surfaces a few shades apart, titles
	in the theme font, hairlines drawn in the text colour, raised fields, and one accent on
	screen (the switch). Ships with the Shannon Dark and Shannon Light presets.
	Returns { Id, Structure, Metrics, derive }. Every colour is a blend of the panel, the text
	colour, black and white, so custom themes keep working.
]]

local Shannon = {}

Shannon.Id = "Shannon"

Shannon.Structure = {
	ChevronSide = "Right",
	TypeHeader = "Plain",
	-- Hairline between type sections.
	TypeRule = 1,
	GroupDivider = true,
	FieldOutline = "Always",
	Toggle = "Switch",
	NumberFont = "Body",
	TitleFont = "Theme",
	TypeFont = "Theme",
	TitleBarFill = false,
	AxisOutline = true,
	RowHover = true,
	Shadow = true,
	TitleWeight = Enum.FontWeight.Regular,
	TypeWeight = Enum.FontWeight.Regular,
	GroupWeight = Enum.FontWeight.Medium,
	LabelWeight = Enum.FontWeight.Regular,
	ValueWeight = Enum.FontWeight.Regular,
}

-- Solid surfaces and strokes.
Shannon.Surface = { PanelAlpha = 0, BlobAlpha = 0, BorderAlpha = 0 }

-- Offsets at UI scale 1, keyed by the theme's text size.
Shannon.Metrics = {
	[12] = {
		Text = 12, TitleText = 16, TypeText = 16, GroupText = 12,
		TitleBar = 40, Search = 28, TypeHead = 32, GroupHead = 24,
		Row = 24, RowGap = 4, RowIndent = 0, LabelWidth = 80, LabelGap = 8,
		PanelPad = 12, FieldPad = 8, GroupBodyTop = 4, GroupGap = 12, OpenGroupGap = 0, TypeGap = 16,
		Corner = 8, BigCorner = 12,
		Swatch = 16, ToggleWidth = 28, ToggleHeight = 16, Knob = 12, AxisPill = 20, IconSlot = 20,
	},
	[16] = {
		Text = 16, TitleText = 20, TypeText = 20, GroupText = 16,
		TitleBar = 44, Search = 32, TypeHead = 36, GroupHead = 28,
		Row = 28, RowGap = 4, RowIndent = 0, LabelWidth = 88, LabelGap = 8,
		PanelPad = 12, FieldPad = 8, GroupBodyTop = 4, GroupGap = 12, OpenGroupGap = 0, TypeGap = 16,
		Corner = 8, BigCorner = 12,
		Swatch = 20, ToggleWidth = 36, ToggleHeight = 20, Knob = 16, AxisPill = 20, IconSlot = 20,
	},
}

local WHITE = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
local BLACK = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)

-- The theme's text colour is used as is once it reaches this contrast on the canvas.
local PRIMARY_FLOOR = 12

function Shannon.derive(inputs, ColorMath)
	local canvas = inputs.panel
	local light = ColorMath.isLight(canvas)

	local field = light and WHITE or ColorMath.mix(canvas, WHITE, 0.046)
	local hover = ColorMath.mix(canvas, BLACK, light and 0.02 or 0.18)
	local pressed = ColorMath.mix(canvas, BLACK, light and 0.04 or 0.47)

	local primary = inputs.text
	if ColorMath.minContrast(primary, { canvas, field }) < PRIMARY_FLOOR then
		local hue, saturation = inputs.text:ToHSV()
		primary = ColorMath.solveTone(hue, saturation * 0.55, { canvas, field }, PRIMARY_FLOOR, light)
	end

	local label = ColorMath.backOff(primary, canvas, light and 0.18 or 0.27, 7, { canvas, hover })
	local secondary = ColorMath.backOff(primary, canvas, light and 0.41 or 0.45, 4.5, { canvas, field, hover })
	local disabled = ColorMath.backOff(primary, canvas, 0.62, 3, { canvas, field })

	-- The accent steps toward the text colour until it stands out from the canvas.
	local accent = inputs.accent
	for _ = 1, 60 do
		if ColorMath.contrast(accent, canvas) >= 3 then
			break
		end
		accent = ColorMath.mix(accent, primary, 0.05)
	end
	local knobOn = ColorMath.contrast(WHITE, accent) >= 3 and WHITE or canvas

	local hairline = ColorMath.mix(canvas, primary, 0.15)

	return {
		Panel = canvas,
		Header = canvas,
		Band = canvas,
		Field = field,
		FieldHover = hover,
		Selected = pressed,
		Sunken = pressed,
		TextPrimary = primary,
		TextHeading = primary,
		TextLabel = label,
		TextSecondary = secondary,
		TextDisabled = disabled,
		Outline = ColorMath.mix(field, primary, 0.15),
		OutlineHover = ColorMath.mix(field, primary, 0.30),
		Focus = ColorMath.mix(field, primary, 0.70),
		Divider = hairline,
		Rule = hairline,
		PanelStroke = hairline,
		Accent = accent,
		OnAccent = knobOn,
		ToggleOn = accent,
		ToggleOff = light and ColorMath.mix(canvas, BLACK, 0.07) or pressed,
		KnobOn = knobOn,
		KnobOff = secondary,
	}
end

return Shannon

--[[
	Slate  -  theme mode for a neutral, compact tool panel: type names on filled bands, groups
	split by hairlines, chevrons on the left, monospace numbers, a checkbox for on/off, and
	fields that gain an outline only on hover or focus.
	Returns { Id, Structure, Metrics, derive }. Surfaces keep the panel's hue at low chroma, so
	the theme shows in the type band, the checkbox and the focus ring.
]]

local Slate = {}

Slate.Id = "Slate"

Slate.Structure = {
	ChevronSide = "Left",
	TypeHeader = "Band",
	TypeRule = 0,
	GroupDivider = true,
	FieldOutline = "Hover",

-- Offsets at UI scale 1, keyed by the theme's text size.
Slate.Metrics = {
	[12] = {
		Text = 12, TitleText = 16, TypeText = 12, GroupText = 12,
		TitleBar = 32, Search = 24, TypeHead = 28, GroupHead = 28,
		Row = 24, RowGap = 4, RowIndent = 20, LabelWidth = 88, LabelGap = 4,

	[16] = {

		TitleBar = 36, Search = 28, TypeHead = 32, GroupHead = 32,

		PanelPad = 8, FieldPad = 8, GroupBodyTop = 0, GroupGap = 0, OpenGroupGap = 8, TypeGap = 8,
		Corner = 4, BigCorner = 8,
		Swatch = 16, ToggleWidth = 20, ToggleHeight = 20, Knob = 16, AxisPill = 20, IconSlot = 20,
	},
}

-- OKLCH lightness per role: dark themes read up from the panel, light themes read down.
local DARK = { Primary = 0.96, Label = 0.87, Secondary = 0.77, Disabled = 0.58, Accent = 0.74 }
local LIGHT = { Primary = 0.22, Label = 0.36, Secondary = 0.45, Disabled = 0.62, Accent = 0.50 }

function Slate.derive(inputs, ColorMath)
	local light = ColorMath.isLight(inputs.panel)
	local panelLightness, panelChroma, panelHue = ColorMath.toOklch(inputs.panel)
	local _, textChroma, textHue = ColorMath.toOklch(inputs.text)
	local _, accentChroma, accentHue = ColorMath.toOklch(inputs.accent)

	local base = light and math.clamp(panelLightness, 0.92, 0.98) or math.clamp(panelLightness, 0.20, 0.30)
	local direction = light and -1 or 1
	local surfaceChroma = math.min(panelChroma * 0.6, 0.035)
	local bandChroma = math.min(accentChroma * 0.5, 0.045)
	local tone = light and LIGHT or DARK

	-- Surface `delta` lightness steps away from the panel, toward the text.
	local function surface(delta)
		return ColorMath.fromOklch(base + direction * delta, surfaceChroma, panelHue)
	end

	local panel = surface(0)
	local field = surface(0.06)
	local fieldHover = surface(0.09)
	local band = ColorMath.fromOklch(base + direction * 0.05, bandChroma, accentHue)

	local primary = ColorMath.fromOklch(tone.Primary, math.min(textChroma * 0.2, 0.02), textHue)
	local label = ColorMath.oklchWithContrast(tone.Label, math.min(textChroma * 0.25, 0.025), textHue, { panel }, 7, light)
	local secondary = ColorMath.oklchWithContrast(tone.Secondary, math.min(textChroma * 0.3, 0.03), textHue, { panel, band, fieldHover }, 4.5, light)
	local disabled = ColorMath.fromOklch(tone.Disabled, math.min(textChroma * 0.3, 0.03), textHue)
	local accent = ColorMath.oklchWithContrast(tone.Accent, math.min(accentChroma, 0.13), accentHue, { panel, field }, 3, light)

	return {
		Panel = panel,
		Header = panel,
		Band = band,
		Field = field,
		FieldHover = fieldHover,
		Selected = surface(0.13),
		Sunken = ColorMath.fromOklch(base - 0.03, surfaceChroma, panelHue),
		TextPrimary = primary,
		TextHeading = primary,
		TextLabel = label,
		TextSecondary = secondary,
		TextDisabled = disabled,
		Outline = field,
		OutlineHover = surface(0.17),
		Focus = accent,
		Divider = surface(0.10),
		Rule = surface(0.10),
		PanelStroke = surface(0.10),
		Accent = accent,
		OnAccent = panel,
		ToggleOn = accent,
		ToggleOff = surface(0.36),
		KnobOn = panel,
		KnobOff = secondary,
	}
end

return Slate
